title: Resolve the four one-off borrowings
description:
Four imports, twelve symbols between them, three files — all small, all in files this tick OWNS.

1. internal/factory/dashboard/view.go:10 -> internal/styles. Uses EIGHT colour constants: ColorTeal, ColorSubtext, ColorRed, ColorPurple, ColorPink, ColorGreen, ColorDim, ColorBlue. Copy them into the dashboard package. Rationale to put in a comment: ticfac's dashboard is its own product surface, and binding two products' visual identity together is a coupling neither wants. If they drift apart later, that is correct, not a bug.

2. internal/factory/setup.go:18 -> internal/github, ONE function: github.DetectProject. Copy it. Do NOT promote internal/github — it handles OAuth device-flow token exchange, and a frozen public API around credential handling is a liability we are explicitly avoiding.

3. internal/cloud/collect/collect.go:31 -> internal/herd/gitcmd, gitcmd.Run x6. A git exec helper. Copy it or use a tk equivalent — decide per call site and say which you chose and why.

4. internal/cloud/collect/collect.go:30 -> internal/herd/collect, TWO refs: collect.Verdict and collect.StatusNeedsContext. A verdict type and a status constant. NOTE: this pair is a shared VOCABULARY between local herd collect and cloud collect — if they diverge, a cloud run and a herd run disagree about what 'needs context' means. Copying is right for the extraction, but the shared meaning is real: say in a comment that the two are intentional twins, and check whether Phase 2's contract artifact should cover them.

Also: internal/factory/dashboard/view_test.go:11 imports internal/herd/dashboard. Test-only. Check whether the reference survives at all once the dashboard owns its own types; delete it if it does not.
acceptance_criteria: internal/factory/** and internal/cloud/** import none of internal/styles, internal/github, internal/herd/gitcmd, internal/herd/collect, internal/herd/dashboard. Each copy carries a comment saying why it is a copy rather than a shared package. The collect.Verdict twin-vocabulary risk is recorded on the Phase 2 epic (kka). go test ./internal/... green.
